feature1.prompt: Enhance the autodoc system’s ability to handle overloaded methods by extracting all method signatures from a docstring. When wrapping C++ classes for Python with SWIG, it is common to have multiple signatures for overloaded methods listed at the start of the docstring. Currently, only the first signature is recognized, leading to incomplete documentation. This feature requires a modification to the signature extraction logic so that every signature present in the docstring is captured and can be later displayed in the documentation output.
feature1.hint_texts: This feature involves modifying the core logic within the _find_signature method in the DocstringSignatureMixin class. Developers should update the iteration over the docstring lines to allow for the extraction of multiple signatures, including handling multi-line signatures and ensuring robust processing of edge cases. Pay special attention to updating the _new_docstrings and _signatures instance variables to store the results of the extraction correctly. The implementation should follow the existing pattern matching using the signature regular expression, but without stopping at the first match.
feature1.entrypoint: File: sphinx/ext/autodoc/__init__.py – Focus on the _find_signature method within the DocstringSignatureMixin class. Modify the code block starting around line 1036 where the docstring is processed, and add logic to collect and store all matching signatures. Ensure that enhancements respect the existing API and integrate seamlessly with the rest of the autodoc module.

tests.FAIL_TO_PASS: No direct unit tests are provided specifically for the core extraction logic; the failure cases for multiple signatures are captured in integration tests.
tests.PASS_TO_PASS: Unit functionality ensuring that the extraction for single signatures continues to work as expected should pass without modification.

feature2.prompt: Update the autodoc documentation generation to integrate support for overloaded methods by correctly displaying multiple signatures. In many cases, especially with SWIG-wrapped C++ classes, methods are overloaded and include several signatures at the beginning of the docstring. The current behavior only shows the first signature, which does not meet the convention. The aim of this feature is to modify the output so that all available signatures are included, providing a complete and accurate representation of the method’s overloads.

Make sure to update the expected results for tests that previously failed due to incomplete signature extraction, while maintaining the behavior of tests that passed.
